synopsis: A high-speed flight through Jupiter's Trojan asteroid field among ancient space rocks.

shots.prompt:
One continuous 15-second first-person flight at 24 fps, filmed as if the camera itself is the spacecraft, moving forward without pause for the entire take. Seconds 0-4 are calm and wide: the real body fills one side of the frame, lit hard from the side, the far sun flaring at the frame edge, and the camera is already drifting forward. Seconds 4-6 accelerate toward the obstacle field and the first objects slide into frame. Seconds 6-13 race through the field itself: objects rush past on both sides and overhead, the nearest ones blurring, fine particles streaking past the lens, objects colliding and bursting apart, the body still showing through the gaps. Seconds 13-15 plunge into the densest part and the frame fills with the climax, the brightest and most overwhelming moment of the whole take, still moving forward as it ends. One continuous take, no cut, no fade, no scene change, and the camera never stops or hovers. Nothing of the vehicle is visible: no cockpit, no hull, no instruments, no HUD. No text, no captions, no logos, no watermark, no people. Sound: diegetic only and locked to what is on screen, a deep low rumble running under the whole flight, quiet and distant at the start, sharp impacts hitting exactly when objects collide, the whole sound field growing continuously and reaching its loudest and fullest in the final two seconds. No music, no voice, no narration.

First-person perspective flying forward through Jupiter's Trojan asteroid field. From seconds 0 to 4, calm wide view of dark pitted asteroids drifting against the massive banded disk of Jupiter filling the background in hard side light. From seconds 4 to 6, camera speeds toward the asteroid cluster as house-sized dark boulders roll into frame. From seconds 6 to 13, rapid navigation through dense rock clusters with rocky debris rushing past on both sides, smaller gravel blurring near the lens, and colliding asteroids shattering into sharp fragments in the gap. From seconds 13 to 15, direct plunge into a high-density boulder field, ending in a bright impact cloud of pulverized rock that fills the frame completely. One continuous take, no cut, no fade, no scene change, and the camera never stops or hovers. Nothing of the vehicle is visible: no cockpit, no hull, no instruments, no HUD. No text, no captions, no logos, no watermark, no people. Sound begins as a distant low bass rumble, rising with sharp metallic rock impacts that reach maximum volume in the final two seconds.

first_comment: How many asteroids do you think exist in Jupiter's orbit? ☄️
caption:
This flight navigates through the Trojan asteroid swarm sharing the orbit of Jupiter.

Thousands of dark rocky bodies measuring from one metre to over two hundred kilometres drift in gravitational balance pockets.

NASA's Lucy spacecraft launched in 2021 to inspect these ancient remnants for clues about planetary formation.

Orbital speeds exceeding twenty kilometres per second turn minor debris collisions into catastrophic impacts capable of vaporising any craft.

This is a simulation, not real footage. Which asteroid field would you explore first if human travel were possible?
